article.Citation/Title: O'Donnell, K. C., Mennenga, S. E., Owens, L. T., Podrebarac, S. K., Baron, T., Rotrosen, J., Ross, S., Forcehimes, A. A., & Bogenschutz, M. P. (2022). Psilocybin for alcohol use disorder: Rationale and design considerations for a randomized controlled trial. Contemporary Clinical Trials, 123, 106976.
article.InterventionDescription: Oral psilocybin 25mg/70kg (titrated) vs. diphenhydramine, two 8-hour sessions (weeks 4, 8), embedded in 12-week manualized PSI+META psychotherapy, academic outpatient sites.
article.EligibilityNote: Protocol/rationale paper for RCT NCT02061293; primary outcomes explicitly stated as 'published elsewhere' (ref 9, Bogenschutz et al. 2022 JAMA Psychiatry). No effect sizes, p-values, or substance-use outcome data are reported in this text -- describes design only. Fails (a): describes rather than reports a trial. Fails (b): no substance-use outcome data reported.

article.EligibleYN: Applied the screen honestly per instructions: this article's Methods/Discussion describe a fully-conducted RCT (96 randomized, 93 dosed at least once) but the abstract and 'Trial status' section state explicitly that primary outcomes 'will be published elsewhere' / 'have been published elsewhere [9]' -- no outcome data, effect size, or substance-use result of any kind appears anywhere in this text. Per task guidance, a rationale-and-design paper describes a trial rather than reporting one, so it fails (a); and because no substance-use outcome is reported anywhere in the text, it also fails (b). Coded EligibleYN='N', EligibilityFailedCriterion='both'.
article.Citation/Title: This is the design/rationale paper for the trial whose primary results are reported in the companion publication: Bogenschutz, M.P., et al. (2022). Percentage of heavy drinking days following psilocybin-assisted psychotherapy vs placebo... JAMA Psychiatry 79(10), 953-962 (ref [9] in this article). Extracted citation elements from the title page/header of the supplied text.
article.Outcome: No effect size is reported anywhere in this text. The article states its primary outcome is 'the proportion of heavy drinking days during the 32 weeks after the first dosing session' (Sec 2.1.1), but explicitly defers all results to the companion publication [9] ('The primary outcomes have been published elsewhere'; 'Trial status' section). Coded '.'.
article.SD: No dispersion or test statistic for any outcome is reported in this text; only the statistical *methods* (MMRM, RM MANOVA) are described (Sec 4.2), with no computed values. Coded '.'.
article.PVal: No p-value is reported anywhere in this text; results are deferred to ref [9]. Coded '.'.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: No analysis is reported in this article, so there is no analyzed-N to record. The text gives only enrollment/randomization counts: 96 participants randomized, 93 of whom received at least one dose of study medication (Sec 3.1) -- these are not an analysis denominator. Coded '.'.
article.Pos Result Y/N: Coded 3 (cannot be determined): no outcome data of any kind is reported in this protocol/design article; directionality of the treatment effect is not stated or determinable from this text.
article.Clincial Trial YN: Coded 0 to avoid the required internal-consistency contradiction with EligibilityFailedCriterion including a failure of criterion (a) (per the prompt: 'Clincial Trial YN = 1 with a failed criterion (a)... is an internal contradiction and will be rejected'). This does not mean no trial was conducted -- NCT02061293 was in fact completed with 96 randomized participants -- only that this particular article does not itself report the trial's conduct or outcomes, so the field is aligned with the eligibility verdict as the schema requires.
article.RandomizationYN: Coded 1 from the described design (randomization was in fact performed: stratified by site, permuted blocks of varied sizes, assigned sequentially by the study pharmacist per Sec 4.1.1), per the boundary-case instruction that design features the protocol specifies may still be coded from the described design despite ineligibility.
article.BlindingYN: Coded 1: the trial is described as double-blind, with study staff (except the pharmacist) blind to treatment arm (Sec 4.1.2), coded from the described design per the boundary-case instruction.
article.Double+Blind: Coded 1, consistent with BlindingYN=1: the article's title, abstract, and Sec 2.1 all describe the trial as 'double-blind.'
article.Comparator: Coded 1: active placebo (diphenhydramine 50-100mg) was used as comparator (Sec 4.1.4, 5.4), coded from the described design per the boundary-case instruction.
article.PrimaryCare: Coded 1 on a narrow basis: Table 1's blood-pressure footnote states participants with mildly elevated BP at screening 'may be provisionally included and referred to their primary care provider for management of hypertension.' This is a single incidental safety-referral touchpoint, not integration of care delivery within a primary-care setting -- a borderline call, flagged here.
article.Power: Coded 0. The article describes a planned enrollment target (100-180) with a planned sample-size re-estimation after 100 randomizations (Sec 3.1), but does not describe a formal a priori or post hoc power calculation, nor state the study was underpowered. No explicit 'power' discussion found in the text.
article.Retention (%): Not calculable: the article reports only randomized N (96) and number who received >=1 dose (93); no study-completion or attrition counts are given (results deferred to ref [9]). Coded '.'.
article.ConfoundYN: Coded 1: the statistical analysis plan (Sec 4.2) explicitly includes fixed covariates, treatment-by-assessment interactions, and planned tests of statistical mediation/moderation of the treatment effect (Aims 3-4) using a product-of-coefficients bootstrapping approach. This reflects planned methodology, not applied/reported adjusted results, since no results appear in this text.
article.BaseStatus: Sample is defined by DSM-IV alcohol dependence diagnosis plus a heavy-drinking-days threshold (Table 1), but no explicit severity grading (e.g., an AUDIT score or stated mild/moderate/severe classification) is given in this text. Coded '.' rather than inferring a severity band from the diagnosis alone.
article.Age_Median: Inclusion criteria specify an eligible age range of 25-65 (Table 1), but no sample mean/median age is reported in this design paper (would appear in the companion results paper). Coded '.'.
article.PercentFem: Not reported in this text; no sample demographic breakdown is given (design paper only).
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: Not reported in this text; no sample demographic breakdown is given (design paper only).
article.Country_USvsNonUS: Both trial sites are in the US: NYU Grossman School of Medicine (New York, NY) and University of New Mexico (Albuquerque, NM), per author affiliations and Sec 2.1.
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Coded 0: recruitment relied substantially on self-referral after participants learned of the study via ClinicalTrials.gov and psychedelic-research-related media/books (Sec 3.2), and the Discussion explicitly notes that the trial's 'rigorous inclusion/exclusion criteria' screened out many prospective participants, 'which may limit generalizability of the results.'
article.Followup in months: Computed as 42 weeks / 4.345 = 9.7 months, measuring from the end of the core 12-week double-blind treatment phase to the final double-blind assessment window culminating in the week-54 visit. This is ambiguous because the design has two treatment endpoints: the double-blind treatment ends at week 12 (with primary-endpoint assessment at week 36), and an optional open-label extension adds further treatment through week 42 before final assessment at week 54. An alternative reading (total protocol duration, week 0 to week 54 = 54 weeks) would give ~12.4 months. Flagged as a judgment call.
article.RelapseMeasured: Coded 0: the article tracks percent heavy drinking days, drinking days, and abstinence longitudinally (Table 2, Sec 4.2), but does not use the term 'relapse' or frame any outcome specifically as relapse/return-to-use tracking.
article.SafetyReported: Coded 'Y': Sec 5.1 ('Safety considerations') and Sec 4.2 explicitly describe a dedicated safety-assessment methodology -- an Adverse Events Case Report Form at nearly every visit (Table 2), vital signs, ECG, and a planned statistical comparison of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) between arms. This satisfies the 'explicit statement/section exists' test, even though no numeric AE results appear in this text.
article.AnyAEReported: Coded 'N': although safety assessment is described in detail as a methodology, no specific adverse event (type, count, or occurrence) for this trial is reported anywhere in this text -- results are explicitly deferred to the companion publication [9]. This is a schema-forced value; it reflects that no AE data is reported IN THIS ARTICLE, not a claim that the trial recorded zero adverse events. Flagged per the prompt's cardinal AE-understatement concern.
article.NumDistinctAEs: Forced to 0 by the rule that NumDistinctAEs=0 only when AnyAEReported='N'. No AE count is actually stated in this text; see the AnyAEReported rationale for the underlying ambiguity.
article.NParticipantsWithAE: Not reported in this text (no AE data given). Coded '.'.
article.AE_denominator: Not reported in this text; no safety-population AE tabulation appears (only the plan to tabulate TEAEs is described). Coded '.', not 'NA', per the rule that '.' applies even when the article discusses safety but gives no analyzable AE denominator.
article.ArmScope: Coded 'NA': no AE values of any kind are reported in this text, so arm scope (psychedelic_arm vs pooled) genuinely does not apply -- there is nothing to scope. Not coded merely because the study has a comparator arm; coded because there is zero AE data.
article.WorstSeverity: Coded 'None' as the mechanical consequence of AnyAEReported='N' per the AE-gate table. Flagged explicitly: this reflects the absence of AE data in this specific article's text, not a clinical finding that no adverse events occurred in the trial -- harms were in fact assessed via a detailed AE-CRF protocol, with results appearing only in the companion publication [9].
article.HarmsAssessed: Coded 1: the study protocol assesses harms as an explicit Aim (Aim 1, safety), with AE-CRF administered at nearly every visit (Table 2) and a planned TEAE tabulation and between-group comparison (Sec 4.2). This is a design/methods fact, true regardless of whether numeric AE results appear in this specific article. Paired with SafetyReported='Y' per the required equivalence.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: Objective (Sec 2.1.1), design (Sec 2.1), setting (NYU/UNM), eligibility (Table 1), intervention (Sec 4.1.2-4.1.4), comparator (Sec 5.4), outcomes (primary/secondary listed in Sec 2.1.1), randomization procedure (Sec 4.1.1), blinding (Sec 4.1.2), statistical methods (Sec 4.2), harms-assessment plan (Sec 5.1, Table 2), and funding/COI (dedicated sections) are all explicitly described. Fails 'sample_size_power' (enrollment target and re-estimation plan given, but no formal power calculation stated) and 'results' (this is a protocol/design paper; all outcome results are explicitly deferred to the companion publication, ref [9]). 12 of 14 met, below the 13-of-14 threshold, so MethodologyDescribedYN=0.
